evidence.explanation: No middleware in chain. Handler reads id from query param and concatenates directly into SQL (db.Query at line 120). Unauthenticated callers can query any user record.

No middleware in chain. Handler extracts :id from URL and executes 'DELETE FROM users WHERE id=?' (db.Exec at line 135) with no authentication or ownership check. Any unauthenticated caller can permanently delete any user row.
userID := c.Param("id") used directly as deletion predicate. Even with authentication, no ownership check compares caller identity to targeted resource ID — horizontal privilege escalation.
No middleware. Accepts arbitrary client_id and scope from unauthenticated callers and stores them in server-side state (StoreAuthRequest) without verifying the requesting user is authenticated.
No middleware. Consent form renders with no session/auth check. code parameter reflected into HTML without escaping (line 180) — also XSS. Any unauthenticated party can drive the consent flow.
No middleware in chain. Token endpoint is unauthenticated (no client authentication).

scopeFromForm read from attacker-controlled POST body. authRequest retrieved (line 220) but its stored Scope is never compared against scopeFromForm. Attacker-supplied scope flows directly to token response — scope escalation to 'admin'.
No middleware. Unauthenticated callers reach the 4-hop SQL injection sink (callChainSQLiHandler chain to db.Query).
authMiddleware always calls c.Next() with no failure-return path. Body is c.Set("user_id", "user123"); c.Next() — no c.Abort(), no 401/403. Identity-setting only, zero enforcement.

recipientID read from c.Query("to") with no ownership/relationship check. Any caller can debit userID and credit any arbitrary recipientID. db.Exec at lines 285-286 executes both sides against attacker-supplied accounts.
authMiddleware always calls c.Next() unconditionally; provides no blocking enforcement for the admin endpoint.

extractUserFromToken (line 301) decodes a JWT but does not validate the IsAdmin claim against any server-side authz service. Handler gates on client-supplied user.IsAdmin (line 319). Attacker forging a token with IsAdmin:true reaches db.Exec at line 321.

weak_primitives.reason: Body is c.Set("user_id", "user123"); c.Next() — always calls Next with no conditional abort, never writes 401/403. Non-blocking identity-setter, not a blocking authz primitive.
